lessons.title: Off the Surface & From Cities - Az asztalról és Budapestről
lessons.grammar: Delative case -ról/-ről; cities and surface origins; question word honnan
goal: I can express movement off a surface using -ról/-ről.
I can say I am arriving from Hungarian cities such as Budapestről and Szegedről.

lessons.title: Talking About Things - Miről beszélünk?
lessons.grammar: Delative case for topic; question pronouns miről and kiről
goal: I can use -ról/-ről to say what topic I am talking, reading, or telling stories about.
I can ask questions using Miről? and Kiről?.

lessons.title: Where Are You Coming From? - Honnan jössz?
lessons.grammar: Three-way source case contrast; origin adverbs messziről and otthonról

I can use origin adverbs like otthonról and messziről.

lessons.title: Travel & Origins - Utazás és érkezés
lessons.grammar: Integrated origin cases; travel vocabulary; narrative reading
goal: I can ask and answer where people and gifts come from in travel contexts.
I can read and understand a story about friends returning from trips.

lessons.title: Speaking Languages - Beszélsz magyarul?
lessons.grammar: Essive-modal suffix -ul/-ül with languages; vowel harmony rules
goal: I can say what languages I speak using the essive-modal suffix -ul/-ül.
I can ask someone if they speak Hungarian or other languages.

lessons.title: Learning and Understanding - Tanulok és értek
lessons.grammar: Verbs with -ul/-ül (tanul, ért, olvas, ír); negation with languages
goal: I can express learning, reading, writing, and understanding in different languages.
I can state whether I find a language easy or difficult.

lessons.title: How Well Do You Speak? - Hogy beszélsz?
lessons.grammar: Adverbs of fluency and degree; aspectual particles már and még
goal: I can describe how well I speak a language (egy kicsit, jól, folyékonyan).
I can use progress particles like már, még, and csak.

lessons.title: Manner & Everyday Expressions - Rosszul és egyedül
lessons.grammar: Manner adverbs with -ul/-ül; adjective vs adverb distinction
goal: I can use idiomatic -ul/-ül manner adverbs such as rosszul, egyedül, and például.
I can distinguish adjectives from their -ul/-ül adverb counterparts.

lessons.title: Language Exchange - Nyelvcsere a kávézóban
lessons.grammar: Meta-communicative phrases; counting languages; story reading
goal: I can participate in a simple language exchange conversation.
I can ask what words mean and how to say phrases in Hungarian.

lessons.title: Under and Above - Alatt és felett
lessons.grammar: Postpositions alatt and felett/fölött; bare nominative noun complement
goal: I can use the postpositions alatt (under) and felett (above) with bare nouns.
I can describe the position of objects in a room.

lessons.title: Next to, In Front of, Behind - Mellett, előtt, mögött
lessons.grammar: Spatial postpositions mellett (beside), előtt (in front of), mögött (behind)
goal: I can describe spatial relationships around town using mellett, előtt, and mögött.
I can give and follow meeting directions relative to landmarks.

lessons.title: Between and After - Között és után
lessons.grammar: Postpositions között (between) and után (after in time and space)
goal: I can use között (between/among) and után (after) in spatial and temporal contexts.
I can describe schedules and street navigation.

lessons.title: Temporal Before & After - Előtt és után időben
lessons.grammar: Temporal postpositions előtt, után, and alatt; time-sequencing
goal: I can express temporal sequences with előtt (before), után (after), and alatt (during).
I can schedule appointments and activities with clock times and events.

lessons.title: Searching the Room - Hol van a jegy?
lessons.grammar: Integrated postpositions in dialogue; searching and locating vocabulary
goal: I can locate missing objects using various spatial postpositions in context.
I can read and understand a story about finding a lost ticket.

lessons.title: My Typical Day - Egy hétköznapi napom
lessons.grammar: Daily routine verbs; Review: -kor with a daily routine
goal: I can describe the main events of a typical day.
I can say what time something happens.

lessons.title: Getting Ready - Készülődés
lessons.grammar: Getting ready verbs; Sequencing with előbb, aztán, utána, végül
goal: I can describe how I get ready in the morning.
I can put steps of a routine in order.

lessons.title: Workdays and Weekends - Hétköznapok és hétvégék
lessons.grammar: Review: days + -on/-en/-ön; hétköznap vs. hétvége, munkanap/szabadnap
goal: I can say what I do on a particular day of the week.
I can contrast weekdays and the weekend.

lessons.title: How Often? - Milyen gyakran?
lessons.grammar: Counting occurrences with -szor/-szer/-ször; "every" as one word with -nta/-nte
goal: I can say how many times something happens.
I can say how often something happens using a single word.

lessons.title: Describing My Routine - A napirendem leírása
lessons.grammar: From ... to ... with -tól/-től ... -ig; putting a routine description together
goal: I can describe a span of time from one point to another.
I can give a connected description of my daily routine.

lessons.title: Days, Weeks and Months - Napok, hetek és hónapok
lessons.grammar: This week, last week, next week; the rest of the months (May-December)
goal: I can say this week, last week, and next week.
I can name all twelve months and say which month something is in.

lessons.title: Dates - Dátumok
lessons.grammar: Ordinal numbers első-tizedik; saying a date with -án/-én
goal: I can count first through tenth.
I can say and ask a date.

lessons.title: When? - Mikor?
lessons.grammar: Stacking time expressions (day + part of day + clock time); making an appointment
goal: I can combine a day, part of the day, and exact time in one sentence.
I can ask about and describe an appointment.

lessons.title: Since When? Until When? - Mettől meddig?
lessons.grammar: -tól/-től ... -ig beyond the clock (days, months); asking a span with mettől meddig?
goal: I can say when something starts using -tól/-től.
I can say when something ends using -ig, and mark a whole span of time.

lessons.title: Making a Schedule - Beosztás készítése
lessons.grammar: Putting a schedule together; beosztás/heti/időbeosztás
goal: I can describe a whole weekly schedule by combining what I've learned.
I can talk about a schedule using beosztás and heti.

lessons.title: My Family - A családom
lessons.grammar: The extended family; describing a family tree
goal: I can name extended family members.
I can describe a simple family tree.

lessons.title: Family Members - Családtagok
lessons.grammar: The 3rd-person possessive suffix -a/-e/-ja/-je ("his/her X"); fiú -> fia irregular
goal: I can say "his/her X" for family members.
I can recognize the fiú -> fia irregular.

lessons.title: My Parents and Grandparents - A szüleim és nagyszüleim
lessons.grammar: Plural-possessed -i ("his/her Xs"); -nál/-nél "at someone's place"
goal: I can say "his/her parents/grandparents/siblings" using -i.
I can say I'm at someone's place using -nál/-nél.

lessons.title: Family Life - Családi élet
lessons.grammar: Family-life verbs (meglátogat, összejön, ünnepel); közeli "close"
goal: I can talk about visiting family and getting together.
I can describe a close family.

lessons.title: A Family Story - Egy családi történet
lessons.grammar: Putting a family story together; izgul "to be nervous"
goal: I can describe a family visit from start to finish.
I can say I'm nervous about something.

lessons.title: What Does He Look Like? - Hogy néz ki?
lessons.grammar: More appearance words (haj, vörös); the -s "having X" adjective suffix
goal: I can describe someone's hair and other features.
I can turn a noun into a "having X" adjective with -s.

lessons.title: Personality - Személyiség
lessons.grammar: More personality words (okos, lusta, szorgalmas, türelmes, barátságos, komoly)
goal: I can describe someone's personality with more detail.
I can combine two personality words in one description.

lessons.title: Similar and Different - Hasonló és különböző
lessons.grammar: hasonló/különböző/egyforma; comparing with olyan, mint
goal: I can say two people or things are similar or different.
I can compare using olyan, mint ("like, as").

lessons.title: What Kind of Person? - Milyen ember?
lessons.grammar: The relative pronoun aki ("who"); ismer "to know (a person)"
goal: I can describe someone using a whole clause with aki.
I can say I know a person with ismer.

lessons.title: Describing Someone - Valaki leírása
lessons.grammar: Putting a full description together; meeting Petra and Tamás
goal: I can give a full description of a new person in my life.
I can introduce a colleague or neighbor with an aki-clause.

lessons.title: My Friends - A barátaim
lessons.grammar: Friends and acquaintances (barátnő, ismerős, közös); nem csak..., hanem... is
goal: I can distinguish a friend from an acquaintance.
I can say someone is not only one thing, but also another.

lessons.title: How We Met - Hogyan ismerkedünk
lessons.grammar: ismerkedik "to get acquainted"; keresztül "through"
goal: I can talk about how people get to know each other.
I can say I met someone through another person.

lessons.title: Getting Along - Jól kijövünk
lessons.grammar: kijön valakivel "to get along"; egymással "with each other"
goal: I can say I get along well (or not) with someone.
I can say two people get along with each other.

lessons.title: Making Friends - Barátkozás
lessons.grammar: barátkozik "to make friends"; nyitott "open"
goal: I can say whether I make friends easily.
I can describe someone as open to new people.

lessons.title: Relationships - Kapcsolatok
lessons.grammar: Putting a friendship together; saját élet "a life of one's own"
goal: I can describe a real friendship from start to finish.
I can say I have a life and friends of my own.

lessons.title: My Home - Az otthonom

goal: I can say what floor I live on.
I can talk about moving into a new home.

lessons.title: Describing a Room - A szoba leírása
lessons.grammar: Furniture with -on/-en/-ön; -on/-en/-ön vs. -ban/-ben
goal: I can describe where furniture is in a room.
I can choose between -on/-en/-ön and -ban/-ben correctly.

lessons.title: Where Are Things? - Hol vannak a dolgok?
lessons.grammar: Three ways to say "at": -ban/-ben, -on/-en/-ön, -nál/-nél
goal: I can choose the right locative suffix for in, on, or at.
I can describe where things are around a home.

lessons.title: Looking for a Flat - Lakáskeresés
lessons.grammar: -ra/-re "onto" (sublative); -ról/-ről "off of" (delative)
goal: I can say I'm putting something onto a surface.
I can say I'm taking something off a surface.

lessons.title: Our New Home - Az új otthonunk
lessons.grammar: Putting a home together: -ban/-ben, -on/-en/-ön, -ra/-re, -ról/-ről
goal: I can describe moving into and arranging a new home.
I can combine all three locative case trios in one description.

goal: I can say I'm going to a place using -hoz/-hez/-höz.
I can name places in my neighbourhood.

goal: I can say what's close to or far from a place.
I can talk about the river and the bridge near me.

lessons.title: Places in the City - Helyek a városban
lessons.grammar: -hoz/-hez/-höz on more nouns (rendőrség, színház, szobor); negyed "district"
goal: I can name more places in the city.
I can say which district something is in.

lessons.title: What Is Where? - Mi hol van?
lessons.grammar: -nál/-nél vs -hoz/-hez/-höz vs -tól/-től "at/to/from"; ide, oda, innen, onnan, honnan
goal: I can say where I am, where I'm going, and where I'm coming from.
I can use ide/oda/honnan to talk about here and there.

lessons.title: Describing a City - A város leírása
lessons.grammar: Putting a neighbourhood description together; forgalmas, nyugodt, modern, kedvenc
goal: I can describe what my neighbourhood is like.
I can talk about my favourite places, confidently and without getting lost.

lessons.grammar: keres "to look for"; talál "to find"; vásárol "to buy"
goal: I can say what I'm looking for in a shop.
I can say whether I can find or buy something.

lessons.grammar: közepes "medium"; túl "too"; zöld and sárga "green, yellow"
goal: I can ask for and describe a size.
I can ask for and describe a colour.

lessons.title: Prices and Quantities - Árak és mennyiségek
lessons.grammar: Numbers past ten; mennyibe kerül and -ért for price
goal: I can use numbers well past twenty for prices and quantities.
I can ask and tell how much something costs.

lessons.title: Comparing Products - Termékek összehasonlítása
lessons.grammar: olyan..., mint... reused for products; akció and kedvezmény
goal: I can compare two products using olyan..., mint...
I can talk about sales and discounts.

lessons.title: Choosing What to Buy - Mit vegyünk?
lessons.grammar: választ "to choose"; biztos "sure"; putting a purchase together
goal: I can choose confidently between products.
I can describe a whole shopping trip from looking to paying.

lessons.title: What Do You Like to Eat? - Mit szeretsz enni?
lessons.grammar: eszik/iszik present tense (indefinite); talking about food in general with étel
goal: I can conjugate eszik and iszik in the present tense.
I can talk about food and drink in general terms.

lessons.title: Meals - Étkezések
lessons.grammar: Extending -szor/-szer/-ször to all numbers; meals of the day with uzsonnázik
goal: I can say how many times a day I do something, with any number.
I can name all four meals of the day.

lessons.title: Eating Habits - Étkezési szokások
lessons.grammar: Combining frequency and eszik/iszik; szokás "habit"
goal: I can describe how often I eat or drink something.
I can talk about an eating habit as my own or my family's.

lessons.title: Hungarian Food - Magyar konyha
lessons.grammar: Definite vs indefinite conjugation, formalized; Hungarian food and spices
goal: I can explain when a verb takes the definite form instead of the indefinite one.
I can talk about Hungarian food and spices.

lessons.title: My Favourite Food - A kedvenc ételem
lessons.grammar: Putting the unit together; ízlik "to taste good"
goal: I can describe a favourite meal from start to finish.
I can say that something tastes good.

lessons.title: Ingredients - Hozzávalók
lessons.grammar: Ingredients and spices (recept, hozzávaló, fűszer); kell hozzá
goal: I can name the main ingredients and spices in a recipe.
I can say how much of something a recipe needs.

lessons.title: Recipes - Receptek
lessons.grammar: -val/-vel: "with" something; cooking tools
goal: I can name basic cooking tools.
I can say what I do something with, using -val/-vel.

lessons.title: Cooking at Home - Főzés Otthon
lessons.grammar: The imperative (regular -j pattern); főzzünk együtt "let's cook together"
goal: I can give a simple cooking instruction using the imperative.
I can suggest cooking together using "let's".

lessons.title: Following Instructions - Kövesd a Receptet
lessons.grammar: The definite imperative; fel and hozzá with a command
goal: I can give a command about a specific, definite thing.
I can use fel and hozzá naturally with a command.

lessons.title: Making a Meal - Egy Étel Elkészítése
lessons.grammar: Putting a recipe together; bele "into it"
goal: I can describe making a traditional Hungarian dish from start to finish.
I can say what goes into a dish using bele.

lessons.title: My Hobbies - Hobbijaim
lessons.grammar: Hobby verbs and their -ni infinitives; szabadidő with possessive suffixes
goal: I can name several common hobbies.
I can say what I like and don't like doing in my free time.

lessons.title: Sports - Sport
lessons.grammar: jár + infinitive for regular activities; óta/éve for duration
goal: I can talk about sports I do regularly.
I can say how long I've been doing a sport.

lessons.title: What Do You Like Doing? - Mit szeretsz csinálni?
lessons.grammar: engem érdekel construction; scale of liking (kedvel, szeret, imád, utál)
goal: I can say what interests me using engem érdekel.
I can express different degrees of liking and disliking something.

lessons.title: How Often Do You Do It? - Milyen gyakran csinálod?
lessons.grammar: Stacking frequency (hetente kétszer); productive -nta/-nte (hétvégente, nyaranta)
goal: I can say exactly how many times a day/week/month I do something.
I can build new frequency words with -nta/-nte.

lessons.title: Weekend Activities - Hétvégi programok
lessons.grammar: Putting a weekend together; attól függ; present tense for weekend plans
goal: I can talk about my weekend plans.
I can say that something depends on the weather or circumstances.

lessons.title: Cinema - Mozi
lessons.grammar: Film genre compounds (akciófilm, vígjáték); -ra/-re for event tickets
goal: I can name different kinds of films.
I can buy tickets for a screening.

lessons.title: Music - Zene
lessons.grammar: Playing an instrument with -on/-en/-ön; kedvenc + possessive noun
goal: I can say what instrument I play.
I can talk about my favourite music, songs, and bands.

lessons.title: Books - Könyvek
lessons.grammar: ami/amit relative pronoun for things; szerintem for giving an opinion
goal: I can describe a book or story using a relative clause with ami.
I can give my opinion about a book using szerintem.

lessons.title: Cultural Events - Kulturális események
lessons.grammar: ajánl + dative for recommending; nyitva/zárva with -tól/-től...-ig for opening hours
goal: I can recommend an exhibition, festival, or event to someone.
I can ask and say whether a place is open or closed, and when.

lessons.title: Going Out - Szórakozás
lessons.grammar: Mit szólsz hozzá? for suggestions; sajnos for polite decline
goal: I can suggest going out and ask what someone thinks.
I can politely decline an invitation and give a reason.

lessons.title: What's the Weather Like? - Milyen az idő?
lessons.grammar: Weather adjectives and idő van; süt/fúj weather verbs
goal: I can ask and say what the weather is like.
I can describe the sun and wind with süt and fúj.

lessons.title: The Four Seasons - A négy évszak
lessons.grammar: Seasons and their irregular time-forms (tavasszal, nyáron, ősszel, télen); intensifiers nagyon/elég/túl
goal: I can name the four seasons and say what happens in each one.
I can use nagyon, elég and túl to say how much.

lessons.title: It's Raining - Esik az eső
lessons.grammar: esik for rain and snow; vizes/száraz
goal: I can say it's raining or snowing.
I can describe wet and dry weather.

lessons.title: Hot and Cold - Meleg és hideg
lessons.grammar: meleg/hideg/hűvös/forró and fok; comparative -bb
goal: I can describe hot, cold and cool weather, and ask how many degrees it is.
I can compare temperatures using the comparative -bb.

lessons.title: Weather and Plans - Időjárás és tervek
lessons.grammar: ha + present tense for weather plans; dative kell nekem
goal: I can say what I'll do depending on the weather, using ha.
I can say what I need for the weather with kell nekem.

lessons.title: Buses and Trams - Busz és villamos
lessons.grammar: felszáll/leszáll with -ra/-re and -ról/-ről; -val/-vel for vehicles
goal: I can talk about buses, trams and the metro.
I can say how I get somewhere using -val/-vel and describe getting on and off.

lessons.title: Buying a Ticket - Jegyvásárlás
lessons.grammar: jegy/bérlet and jegyet vált; -ra/-re for validity duration
goal: I can buy a ticket or a pass.
I can ask the price and how long a ticket or pass is valid.

lessons.title: Timetables - Menetrend
lessons.grammar: indul/érkezik; distributive -nként
goal: I can ask when a bus or tram departs and arrives.
I can say how often a bus or tram runs.

lessons.title: Changing Lines - Átszállás
lessons.grammar: átszáll and vonal; hányas question word
goal: I can talk about changing lines.
I can ask which-numbered bus or tram to take.

lessons.title: Getting There - Hogyan jutok oda?
lessons.grammar: hogyan jutok el; hova kell menni + infinitive directions; combining the unit's vocabulary in a door-to-door route
goal: I can ask how to get to a place by public transport.
I can give simple step-by-step directions using a bus, tram or metro.

lessons.title: Planning a Trip - Utazást tervezünk
lessons.grammar: Travel planning vocabulary; múlva ("in [time]"); -ig for duration
goal: I can talk about my travel plans for the near future.
I can say how long I'm going somewhere for.

lessons.title: At the Station - A pályaudvaron
lessons.grammar: Station vocabulary; indul/érkezik with case suffixes; -ig for "as far as"
goal: I can ask when and from where a train departs and arrives.
I can talk about a ticket, a platform, and a connection.

lessons.title: At the Airport - A repülőtéren
lessons.grammar: Airport vocabulary; kell + infinitive; -nál/-nél vs -on/-re for places
goal: I can name the key things and places at an airport.
I can say what you have to do to get through the airport.

lessons.title: Travel Problems - Utazási problémák
lessons.grammar: Travel problem vocabulary; ha ..., akkor ... (real conditions); van/nincs with problems
goal: I can describe a common travel problem.
I can say what happens if something goes wrong.

lessons.title: Talking About a Trip - Utazásról beszélünk
lessons.grammar: Travel preference vocabulary; szeret/utál/imád + infinitive; azért, mert
goal: I can say what I like and hate about traveling.
I can give a reason for a travel preference.

lessons.title: Booking a Room - Szobát foglalunk
lessons.grammar: Hotel room vocabulary; -ra/-re for a number of nights; superlative with leg-
goal: I can ask about room types and say how many nights I want to stay.
I can ask for the best or the cheapest room.

lessons.title: At the Hotel - A szállodában
lessons.grammar: Reception vocabulary; ad + dative + accusative (giving someone something); ordinals with -on/-en/-ön for floors
goal: I can check in and get my key at reception.
I can ask what floor my room is on.

lessons.title: The Room - A szoba
lessons.grammar: Hotel room amenities; -s suffix for 'with X' (klímás, erkélyes); comparative for comparing two rooms
goal: I can describe what's in my hotel room.
I can compare two rooms and say which I prefer.

lessons.title: Problems at the Hotel - Problémák a szállodában
lessons.grammar: Hotel problem vocabulary; nem működik for something not working; kérek egy másikat for a replacement
goal: I can report that something in my room doesn't work.
I can politely ask for a replacement or a different room.

lessons.title: Checking Out - Kijelentkezés
lessons.grammar: Check-out vocabulary; elégedett vagyok valamivel (satisfied with something); kártyával vagy készpénzzel for payment
goal: I can check out and say how I'd like to pay.
I can say whether I was satisfied with my stay.

lessons.title: Parts of the Body - Testrészek
lessons.grammar: Body-part vocabulary (fej, kéz, láb, szem, fül, száj); the fáj construction with possessive suffixes
goal: I can name the main parts of the body.
I can say that a body part hurts.

lessons.title: I Don't Feel Well - Rosszul Vagyok
lessons.grammar: Reflexive érzem magam; symptom vocabulary; the have-pattern with symptoms (lázam van)
goal: I can say how I'm feeling, well or unwell.
I can describe basic symptoms like a fever or a cough.

lessons.title: What's Wrong? - Mi a Baj?
lessons.grammar: Question patterns for symptoms (Mi a baj?, Mi fáj?, Hol fáj?); duration with -ja/-je (két napja)
goal: I can ask someone what's wrong and where it hurts.
I can say how long I've had a symptom.

lessons.title: At the Doctor - Az Orvosnál
lessons.grammar: Doctor's-office vocabulary; formal questions (Mi a panasza?); felír "to prescribe"
goal: I can describe my symptoms formally to a doctor.
I can understand and use basic doctor's-office vocabulary.

lessons.title: At the Pharmacy - A Gyógyszertárban
lessons.grammar: Putting the unit together; ellen "against"; pharmacy vocabulary and dosage instructions
goal: I can ask for something for a specific ailment at the pharmacy.
I can understand basic dosage instructions.

lessons.title: Healthy Habits - Egészséges Szokások
lessons.grammar: Healthy-living vocabulary; quantity adverbs sokat/eleget; alszik as an -ik verb
goal: I can describe healthy and unhealthy habits.
I can say how much I exercise and sleep.

lessons.title: What Should I Do? - Mit Tegyek?
lessons.grammar: kellene for soft advice; the 1st-person imperative as "what should I do?" (Mit csináljak?, Mit tegyek?)
goal: I can say what someone should do using kellene.
I can ask what I should do in a situation.

lessons.title: Giving Advice - Tanácsadás
lessons.grammar: helyett for doing one thing instead of another; azt javaslom/tanácsolom, hogy + imperative for advice given to someone else
goal: I can say I do one thing instead of another using helyett.
I can give advice to someone else using azt javaslom/tanácsolom, hogy.

lessons.title: What Can I Do? - Mit Tudok Csinálni?
lessons.grammar: tud + infinitive for personal ability; lehet + infinitive for general possibility/permission
goal: I can say what I am and am not able to do using tud.
I can say what is or isn't possible or allowed using lehet.

lessons.title: Better Habits - Jobb Szokások
lessons.grammar: irregular comparative jó/jobb, jól/jobban; mostantól for committing to a new habit
goal: I can compare habits using jobb, rosszabb and egészségesebb.
I can say how I'm changing my habits from now on.

lessons.title: School and University - Iskola és egyetem
lessons.grammar: jár + -ba/-be/-ra/-re for attending school; X óta for 'since'
goal: I can talk about school and university life using words like tanár, diák, and vizsga.
I can say where I study and since when.

lessons.title: Subjects - Tantárgyak
lessons.grammar: jó/rossz + -ban/-ben for skill areas; tanul with a definite object
goal: I can name school subjects and say which ones I'm good or bad at.
I can say what I'm studying, in general or for a specific exam.

lessons.title: Learning Languages - Nyelvtanulás
lessons.grammar: -ul/-ül for speaking 'in' a language; tud for knowing a language and simple ability
goal: I can say what languages I speak, using the correct -ul/-ül form.
I can say what I can and can't do in a language with tud.

lessons.title: How Do You Learn? - Hogyan tanulsz?
lessons.grammar: Manner adverbs with -an/-en; action nouns + -val/-vel for learning methods
goal: I can describe how I learn, quickly or slowly, easily or with difficulty.
I can say what methods I use to learn, like practicing or repeating.

lessons.title: My Language Goals - A nyelvtanulási céljaim
lessons.grammar: Present tense with a future time word for plans; hogy-clauses with remélem and a célom for hopes and goals
goal: I can talk about my language-learning plans using the present tense with a future time word.
I can express my hopes and goals with remélem and a célom, hogy...

lessons.title: Free Time & Culture - Szabadidő és kultúra
lessons.grammar: review leisure/hobby vocabulary and culture-related activities
goal: I can talk about my hobbies, sports and how often I do them.
I can suggest going out, talk about culture, and politely decline an invitation.

lessons.title: Weather & Getting Around - Időjárás és közlekedés
lessons.grammar: review weather/seasons vocabulary and public transport
goal: I can describe the weather and the seasons, and make weather-based plans.
I can get around town by bus, tram or metro, and ask for directions.

lessons.title: Travel & Staying Somewhere - Utazás és szállás
lessons.grammar: review travel/holiday vocabulary and hotel/accommodation language
goal: I can plan a trip, deal with travel problems, and talk about my travel experiences.
I can book a hotel room, check in and out, and report a problem with my room.

lessons.title: Health & Feeling Well - Egészség és jólét
lessons.grammar: review health/body vocabulary and healthy-living advice
goal: I can describe symptoms, say what hurts, and talk to a doctor or pharmacist.
I can talk about healthy habits and give or ask for advice.

lessons.title: School, Language & Putting It All Together - Iskola, nyelv és összefoglalás
lessons.grammar: review school/language-learning vocabulary and integrate units 11-19
goal: I can talk about school, university and my language-learning progress.
I can combine vocabulary and grammar from across Units 11-19 in one connected story.

lessons.title: Jobs and Professions - Foglalkozások
lessons.grammar: X vagyok with no article for professions; possessive suffixes on foglalkozás
goal: I can name common professions in Hungarian, like tanár, orvos, and mérnök.
I can say what my job is with X vagyok, and ask Mi a foglalkozásod?

lessons.title: My Work - A munkám
lessons.grammar: -ban/-ben (and -on/-en/-ön) for where you work; -nál/-nél for who you work for
goal: I can say where I work using egy irodában, egy boltban, and similar phrases.
I can name who I work for with Kinél dolgozol? and -nál/-nél.

lessons.title: A Typical Workday - Egy tipikus munkanap
lessons.grammar: kezdődik/végződik for working hours; accusative for duration (Hány órát dolgozol?)
goal: I can describe my workday using felkelek, dolgozom, and other routine verbs from Unit 1.
I can say my working hours and how long I work using -tól/-től...-ig and the accusative.

lessons.title: Colleagues - Munkatársak
lessons.grammar: Possessive suffixes on workplace nouns; accusative stacked after a possessive suffix
goal: I can talk about my coworkers using possessive suffixes, like a munkatársam and a főnököm.
I can introduce and describe a colleague, like Bemutatom a munkatársamat.

lessons.title: Activities at Work - Tevékenységek a munkahelyen
lessons.grammar: Accusative objects for work tasks (jelentést ír); kell + infinitive marked for a person (Kell dolgoznom)
goal: I can talk about common work tasks like writing a report or sending an email.
I can say what I have to do at work using kell with a personal-marked infinitive, like Kell dolgoznom.

lessons.title: Going In and Going Out - Bemegy és kijön
lessons.grammar: be-/ki- verb prefixes with megy/jön + -ba/-be/-ból/-ből
goal: I can say when someone goes in or comes out of a place using bemegy, bejön, kimegy, and kijön.
I can pair the be-/ki- prefixes with the right -ba/-be or -ból/-ből destination.

lessons.title: Getting Up and Sitting Down - Felkelek és leülök
lessons.grammar: fel-/le- verb prefixes: felkel, lefekszik, leül, felül
goal: I can talk about getting up, sitting down, and lying down using felkel, lefekszik, leül, and felül.
I can recognize fel- and le- as the "up" and "down" prefixes inside verbs I already know.

lessons.title: Starting and Finishing - Elkezdem és befejezem
lessons.grammar: el- and be- as aspectual prefixes: elkezd, elindul, befejez
goal: I can say when I start and finish something using elkezd and befejez.
I can say when I set off or depart using elindul.

lessons.title: Doing Something Completely - Megcsinálom
lessons.grammar: meg- as a completive prefix: megcsinál, megeszik, megiszik vs. the bare verb
goal: I can say I get something completely done using megcsinál.
I can say I finish eating or drinking something using megeszik and megiszik, and tell that apart from the general eszik and iszik.

lessons.title: Where Does the Prefix Go? - Hova kerül az igekötő?
lessons.grammar: Word order: prefix glued to the verb in statements, prefix after the verb with nem
goal: I can keep a verb prefix glued to the front of the verb in a plain statement.
I can put nem before the bare verb and move the prefix after it to make a prefixed verb negative.

lessons.title: I Can... - Tudok...
lessons.grammar: tud + infinitive for a wider range of skills; jól/rosszul + tud to grade a skill
goal: I can talk about a wider range of skills using tud, like driving, cooking, and playing an instrument.
I can say how well I do something using jól/rosszul with tud.

lessons.title: I Can't... - Nem tudok...
lessons.grammar: nem tud + infinitive with mert for reasons; nem tud vs. nem lehet
goal: I can say I'm not able to do something and explain why using nem tud + infinitive and mert.
I can tell apart nem tud (lacking ability) from nem lehet (the situation makes it impossible).

lessons.title: Is It Possible? - Lehet...?
lessons.grammar: lehet + infinitive as a question and its answer; lehet with time, place and frequency
goal: I can ask whether something is possible using Lehet + infinitive, and answer with Igen, lehet / Nem, nem lehet.
I can say when and where something is possible using time, place and frequency words with lehet.

lessons.title: Is It Allowed? - Szabad...?
lessons.grammar: szabad + infinitive for rule-based permission; nem szabad as a strong prohibition
goal: I can ask and say what's allowed by a rule using szabad + infinitive.
I can use nem szabad to state a strong prohibition, and tell it apart from a milder nem lehet.

lessons.title: What Can We Do? - Mit Tudunk Csinálni?
lessons.grammar: tud/lehet/szabad combined; -hat/-het as a one-word preview of "may/can"
goal: I can combine tud, lehet, and szabad in one conversation about plans, choosing the right one for ability, possibility, or permission.
I can recognize a few common -hat/-het forms, like mehetek, as a one-word alternative to lehet + infinitive.

lessons.title: Yesterday - Tegnap
lessons.grammar: Past tense indefinite conjugation for regular verbs, with tegnap and other past time words
goal: I can form the past tense of regular verbs in all persons (indefinite conjugation).
I can say what happened yesterday using tegnap and other past time words.

lessons.title: Last Weekend - Múlt hétvégén
lessons.grammar: Past tense of weekend-activity verbs (kirándul, piknikezik, sportol); múlt hétvégén; group subjects take 3rd person plural
goal: I can talk about weekend activities in the past tense using kirándul, piknikezik and sportol.
I can say múlt hétvégén and use the correct verb form when two people are named together.

lessons.title: What Did You Do? - Mit csináltál?
lessons.grammar: Past-tense questions with mit/kivel/miért; the definite vs indefinite object distinction applies identically in the past
goal: I can ask and answer past-tense questions like Mit csináltál? and Kivel beszéltél?
I can use definite and indefinite verb forms correctly in the past tense.

lessons.title: Where Were You? - Hol voltál?
lessons.grammar: van in the past tense: voltam/voltál/volt/voltunk/voltatok/voltak
goal: I can use volt, the past tense of van, in all persons.
I can ask and answer Hol voltál? and negate volt with nem.

lessons.title: What Happened? - Mi történt?
lessons.grammar: Past tense of megy, jön, eszik and iszik (ment, jött, evett/ette, ivott/itta)
goal: I can use the past tense of megy and jön (ment, jött) in all persons.
I can use the past tense of eszik and iszik (evett/ette, ivott/itta), indefinite and definite.

lessons.title: What Did You Buy? - Mit Vettél?
lessons.grammar: vesz past tense — indefinite vettem vs. definite megvettem
goal: I can say what I bought using vettem (something) vs. megvettem (that specific thing).
I can conjugate vesz through the full past tense, indefinite and definite.

lessons.title: Who Did You Meet? - Kivel Találkoztál?
lessons.grammar: találkozik + -val/-vel in the past; full past of lát
goal: I can say who I met using találkozik + -val/-vel, and ask Kivel találkoztál?
I can conjugate lát in the past, for something unspecified or something specific.

lessons.title: What Did You See? - Mit Láttál?
lessons.grammar: adjective + accusative object; choosing indefinite vs. definite past
goal: I can describe what I bought or saw with an adjective, keeping the adjective bare and putting the case ending only on the noun.
I can choose indefinite or definite past endings correctly based on whether the object is specific.

lessons.title: What Did You Do With It? - Mit Csináltál Vele?
lessons.grammar: past tense + -val/-vel; hazavisz, elad, eltesz
goal: I can ask and answer Mit csináltál vele? about something I bought, found, or met.
I can describe what happened to something afterward using hazavisz, elad, and eltesz.

lessons.title: Talking About Past Events - Elmesélni, Mi Történt
lessons.grammar: connecting past clauses with aztán, utána, előbb...aztán...végül
goal: I can connect several past-tense events with aztán and utána.
I can tell a short story about my day using előbb...aztán...végül and később.

lessons.title: A Day That Went Wrong - Egy Nap, Ami Rosszul Sikerült
lessons.grammar: elkésik, elveszít past tense; sajnos vs. szerencsére in a story
goal: I can say I was late for something using elkésik, and that I lost something using elveszít.
I can narrate a day that went wrong using sajnos and szerencsére together with aztán and utána.

lessons.title: A Funny Story - Egy Vicces Történet
lessons.grammar: nevet past tense + superessive; humor vocabulary in a comic anecdote
goal: I can say I laughed, and what I laughed at, using nevet + the superessive case.
I can tell a short funny story using aztán and utána to build toward the punchline.

lessons.title: My Last Trip - Az Utolsó Utam
lessons.grammar: utazik past tense; amikor for setting the scene of a story
goal: I can talk about a past trip using the new verb utazik.
I can set the scene of a story with amikor and a past-tense clause.

lessons.title: Something That Happened - Valami, Ami Történt
lessons.grammar: egyszer csak / váratlanul + elkezd + infinitive for surprises; azt mondta, hogy... for reported speech
goal: I can describe a surprising event using egyszer csak or váratlanul with elkezd and an infinitive.
I can report what someone said using azt mondta, hogy...

lessons.title: Telling a Short Story - Egy Rövid Történet
lessons.grammar: az elején / a végén to frame a story; combining the unit's connectors into one narrative
goal: I can frame a story using az elején and a végén, alongside the sequencing words I already know.
I can tell a complete short story that combines several storytelling tools from this unit.

lessons.title: Tomorrow - Holnap
lessons.grammar: fog + infinitive for the general future (1st/2nd/3rd singular); contrasted with present tense for scheduled plans
goal: I can build the future tense with fog and a plain infinitive, for I/you/he/she.
I can choose between the present tense and fog + infinitive depending on how certain or fixed a plan is.

lessons.title: Next Week - Jövő héten
lessons.grammar: fog + infinitive across all six persons; present tense vs. fog with jövő héten
goal: I can conjugate fog + infinitive for we/you (pl.)/they, as well as I/you/he/she.
I can use jövő héten with either the present tense or fog + infinitive depending on how fixed the plan is.

lessons.title: My Plans - A terveim
lessons.grammar: tervez + infinitive for active plans; tervez vs. fog vs. gondolkodik
goal: I can say what I'm planning to do using tervez + infinitive.
I can choose between tervez, fog, and gondolkodik depending on how settled a plan really is.

lessons.title: What Will You Do? - Mit fogsz csinálni?
lessons.grammar: Questions with fog + infinitive; negating the future with nem fogok
goal: I can ask what someone will do using fog + infinitive.
I can say what I won't do using nem fogok + infinitive.

lessons.title: Planning the Future - A jövő tervezése
lessons.grammar: Combining present-for-future, fog + infinitive, and tervez + infinitive; majd as a loose future-time adverb
goal: I can pick the right construction — present tense, fog, or tervez — for what I want to say about the future.
I can use majd for a loose, unspecified future time.

lessons.title: Shall We? - Menjünk?
lessons.grammar: -junk/-jünk as a suggestion ("Shall we...?"); accepting, declining, and offering alternatives
goal: I can suggest doing something together using the -junk/-jünk imperative as a question.
I can accept, decline, or offer an alternative to a suggestion.

lessons.title: I Would Like... - Szeretnék...
lessons.grammar: szeretnék unpacked as the conditional -nék; the -nék ending generalized to other verbs, regular and irregular
goal: I can explain that szeretnék is szeret plus the conditional ending -nék.
I can say "I would..." using the -nék ending on other common verbs.

lessons.title: You Should... - Kellene Neked...
lessons.grammar: neked/neki kellene for advice aimed at someone; the 2nd-person conditional (-nál/-nél) as a gentler suggestion
goal: I can aim advice at a specific person using neked/neki kellene.
I can give gentle advice using the 2nd-person conditional (-nál/-nél).

lessons.title: The Full Pattern - Csinálnék, Csinálnál, Csinálna
lessons.grammar: the complete conditional paradigm (-nék/-nál/-na/-nánk/-nátok/-nának) for regular and irregular verbs
goal: I can conjugate a regular verb in the conditional for every person, not just I and you.
I can use the conditional of common irregular verbs like tesz and megy in every person.

lessons.title: If I Had Time... - Ha Lenne Időm...
lessons.grammar: ha + conditional in both clauses for hypothetical "if" sentences; jobb lenne/jó lenne, ha... for wishing a situation were different
goal: I can build a hypothetical "if" sentence using ha with the conditional in both clauses.
I can wish a situation were different using jobb lenne, ha... and jó lenne, ha...

lessons.title: I Think... - Szerintem...
lessons.grammar: azt hiszem and gondolom for introducing an opinion, alongside szerintem
goal: I can introduce an opinion with szerintem, azt hiszem, or gondolom.
I can ask someone what they think, and tell them they're right.

lessons.title: I Prefer... - Inkább...
lessons.grammar: inkább for choosing this over that; jobban szeretem for liking one thing better
goal: I can say what I'd rather do with inkább, and what I'd rather do than something else.
I can say which of two things I like better with jobban szeretem.

lessons.title: Which Is Better? - Melyik jobb?
lessons.grammar: -bb + mint extended to comparing named things; leg- superlative and egyformán for equal comparisons
goal: I can compare two named things, like restaurants or films, and ask which one is better.
I can pick the best of several things, or say two things are equally good.

lessons.title: I Agree / I Don't Agree - Egyetértek / Nem értek egyet
lessons.grammar: egyetért + -val/-vel for agreeing with someone; egyet splits behind the verb under negation
goal: I can say I agree or disagree with someone using egyetért and nem értek egyet.
I can echo someone's opinion briefly with szerintem is or szerintem nem.

lessons.title: Giving Reasons - Indoklás
lessons.grammar: mert and azért, mert reused to justify an opinion, plus Miért gondolod ezt?
goal: I can back up an opinion with a reason using mert.
I can give a more emphatic reason with azért, mert, and ask someone why they think something.

lessons.title: Work & Getting Things Done - Munka és igekötők
lessons.grammar: review job/workplace vocabulary and verb prefixes (be-, ki-, fel-, le-, el-, meg-)
goal: I can talk about my job, where I work, and my workday, using possessive suffixes and cases.
I can use verb prefixes like be-, ki-, fel-, le-, el- and meg- to describe everyday actions, including in the negative.

lessons.title: What You Can and Can't Do - Mit tudsz, mit lehet, mit szabad
lessons.grammar: review tud/lehet/szabad and -hat/-het for ability, possibility and permission
goal: I can say what I'm able to do, and explain why I can't, using tud + infinitive.
I can distinguish between tud, lehet and szabad, and use nem szabad for a strong prohibition.

lessons.title: Talking About the Past - A múlt és a történetek
lessons.grammar: review the past tense (regular and irregular) and storytelling connectors
goal: I can talk about what I did, ate, drank, bought, saw and where I was, using the past tense with the definite/indefinite distinction.
I can tell a short story about the past using connectors like aztán, amikor, and egyszer csak.

lessons.title: The Future & What You'd Do - A jövő és a feltételes mód
lessons.grammar: review the future (fog, tervez, majd) and the conditional mood
goal: I can talk about the future with fog + infinitive, tervez + infinitive, and majd, and negate the future.
I can use the conditional mood (-nék/-nál/-na...) to make suggestions, give advice, and talk about hypothetical situations with ha.

lessons.title: Opinions & Putting It All Together - Vélemények és összefoglalás
lessons.grammar: review opinions, preferences and comparisons, and integrate units 21-29
goal: I can give my opinion, say what I prefer, compare things, and agree or disagree, backing it up with a reason.
I can combine vocabulary and grammar from across Units 21-29 in one connected conversation.

lessons.title: Something Is Wrong - Valami nem stimmel
lessons.grammar: nem működik and elromlott (past of elromlik) for reporting a problem; hiányzik for something missing
goal: I can report that something doesn't work or broke, using nem működik and elromlott.
I can say something is missing, using hiányzik.

lessons.title: Asking for Help - Segítségkérés
lessons.grammar: tudna/tudnál segíteni for polite requests with the conditional; szükségem van valamire for saying what I need
goal: I can politely ask someone if they could help me, using tudna/tudnál segíteni.
I can say I need help or something else, using szükségem van valamire.

lessons.title: Making a Complaint - Reklamálok
lessons.grammar: szeretnék reklamálni for opening a complaint; lehet + infinitive to ask about refunds and exchanges
goal: I can make a complaint and explain the problem, using szeretnék reklamálni.
I can ask about a refund or exchange, using lehet cserélni and kérek egy visszatérítést.

lessons.title: Making and Changing an Appointment - Időpontot Foglalok és Módosítok
lessons.grammar: fog + infinitive for the future tense; időpontot foglalni/módosítani/lemondani for booking, changing, and canceling an appointment
goal: I can talk about the future using fog + infinitive.
I can book, change, or cancel an appointment, using időpontot foglalni, módosítani, and lemondani.

lessons.title: Solving an Everyday Problem - Egy Mindennapi Probléma Megoldása
lessons.grammar: megold/megoldódik for solving a problem; ezért for linking a problem to a request or solution
goal: I can describe a problem, ask for help, and get it solved in one connected exchange.
I can talk about a problem getting solved using megold and megoldódik.

lessons.title: A Day in Hungary - Egy nap Magyarországon
lessons.grammar: connect a full day, present and past, using Units 1-2 and 24-25 together
goal: I can describe a whole day in Hungarian, from morning to night, linking the parts with time words.
I can tell someone what I did yesterday, weaving several actions together in natural past tense.

lessons.title: Family, Friends and Home - Család, barátok és otthon
lessons.grammar: combine family, friends and home vocabulary from Units 3, 5 and 6 in fuller sentences
goal: I can talk about my family, friends and home together in fuller, more natural sentences.
I can describe where people live, and tell the story of a family get-together in the past.

lessons.title: Shopping and Eating - Vásárlás és étkezés
lessons.grammar: combine shopping, food and cooking from Units 8-10 in one connected everyday scenario
goal: I can describe going shopping for ingredients and cooking a meal, from market to table.
I can order food at a restaurant, and tell the story of a meal out afterward.

lessons.title: Work and Free Time - Munka és szabadidő
lessons.grammar: contrast work (Unit 21) and free time (Unit 11) in the same connected sentences
goal: I can describe a work day in detail, using colleagues, tasks and my schedule together.
I can contrast my workdays with my weekends, and tell what I did in my free time.

lessons.title: When Something Goes Wrong - Ha Valami Elromlik
lessons.grammar: combine problem-reporting and polite requests from Unit 31 with past-tense storytelling to explain, solve, and recount an everyday hiccup
goal: I can explain what's wrong when something breaks or stops working, and ask politely for help.
I can tell the story of how I solved the problem myself, and say how confident I've become living in Hungarian.

lessons.title: In Me, In You - Bennem, benned, benne
lessons.grammar: Inessive personal pronouns; verbs governing inessive (bízik, csalódik)
goal: I can use inessive personal pronouns (bennem, benned, benne...) accurately.
I can express trust and certainty using bízik and biztos benne.

lessons.title: On Me, On You - Rajtam, rajtad, rajta
lessons.grammar: Superessive personal pronouns; clothing expressions and dependency idiom múlik
goal: I can use superessive personal pronouns (rajtam, rajtad, rajta...) in context.
I can describe clothing worn and use idioms like rajtad múlik and rajtam a sor.

lessons.title: Look at Me, Wait for Me - Rám, rád, rá
lessons.grammar: Sublative personal pronouns; verbs governing sublative (vár, gondol, szüksége van)
goal: I can use sublative personal pronouns (rám, rád, rá...) with verbs of direction, waiting, and thought.
I can express need using szüksége van rá.

lessons.title: In Us or On Us? - Bennünk vagy rajtunk?
lessons.grammar: Comparison of inessive, superessive, and sublative pronouns; counting on someone (számít rá)
goal: I can contrast inessive, superessive, and sublative personal pronouns.
I can express mutual reliance using számít rá.

lessons.title: Before the Big Exam - Egy fontos vizsga előtt
lessons.grammar: Integrated personal pronouns in supportive dialogue; focus word order
goal: I can offer encouragement and moral support using declined pronouns.
I can read and understand a narrative about friends supporting each other.

lessons.title: At My Place, With Me - Nálam, nálad, nála
lessons.grammar: Adessive personal pronouns; immediate physical possession vs general ownership
goal: I can use adessive pronouns (nálam, nálad, nála...) to say who has an item right now.
I can invite friends over or say whose house an event is at.

lessons.title: Come Over to My Place - Hozzám, hozzád, hozzá
lessons.grammar: Allative personal pronouns; movement towards people and invitations
goal: I can use allative personal pronouns (hozzám, hozzád, hozzá...) to invite people over.
I can describe directional movement toward people using approach verbs.

lessons.title: From Me, From You - Tőlem, tőled, tőle
lessons.grammar: Ablative personal pronouns; verbs of requesting (kér) and receiving (kap)
goal: I can use ablative personal pronouns (tőlem, tőled, tőle...) with verbs of requesting, receiving, and departing.
I can ask favors and inquire about gifts and sources.

lessons.title: About Me, About You - Rólam, rólad, róla
lessons.grammar: Delative personal pronouns; the full three-way person/proximity case paradigm
goal: I can use delative personal pronouns (rólam, rólad, róla...) to discuss people and topics.
I can summarize the three-way proximity case trio (hozzá, nála, tőle).

lessons.title: Hosting Friends - Vendégség a barátoknál
lessons.grammar: Integrated proximity pronoun system (hozzá, nála, tőle); hospitality etiquette
goal: I can interact naturally as a guest or host using the proximity pronoun system.
I can read and understand a story about a Hungarian dinner party.

units.title: Change of State: The Translative Case

lessons.title: Becoming Something: The Translative -vá / -vé
lessons.grammar: Translative-factitive case (-vá / -vé); consonant assimilation
goal: I can form the translative-factitive case (-vá / -vé) with vowel stems.
I can apply consonant assimilation correctly when adding -vá / -vé.

lessons.title: Verbs of Becoming: Válik Valamivé
lessons.grammar: Conjugation and usage of 'válik' + -vá/-vé
goal: I can conjugate and use 'válik' with the translative case.
I can describe transformations and personal developments over time.

lessons.title: Making and Transforming: Tesz Valamivé
lessons.grammar: Factitive use of 'tesz' + -vá/-vé; transformation verbs
goal: I can use 'tesz' with translative adjectives to express causation (making something X).
I can describe renovations and physical conversions using 'átalakít'.

lessons.title: Physical and Natural Transformations
lessons.grammar: Physical changes of state with -vá/-vé
goal: I can talk about natural changes of state such as freezing, melting, and burning.
I can describe daylight and weather transitions.

lessons.title: Idiomatic Expressions & The New Workshop
lessons.grammar: Idiomatic translative expressions; comprehensive narrative
goal: I can use idioms with the translative case such as 'valósággá válik' and 'kővé dermed'.
I can understand a story about a community workshop renovation.

lessons.title: Roles and Professions: The Essive-Formal -ként
lessons.grammar: Essive-formal case (-ként); roles and professions
goal: I can use the invariant suffix -ként to express roles and capacities.
I can describe job functions and volunteer activities using -ként dolgozik.

lessons.title: Life Stages and Perspectives: Gyerekként, Felnőttként
lessons.grammar: Life stages and perspective expressions with -ként
goal: I can describe stages of life using 'gyerekként' and 'felnőttként'.
I can communicate from personal and social perspectives (barátként, külföldiként).

lessons.title: Function and Purpose: Ajándékként, Példaként
lessons.grammar: Function and purpose expressions with -ként
goal: I can describe the intended function or purpose of objects using -ként.
I can use expressions such as 'ajándékként' and 'emlékként' in social situations.

lessons.title: Temporal and Distributive Adverbs: Időnként, Helyenként
lessons.grammar: Temporal and distributive adverbs ending in -ként
goal: I can use temporal adverbs like 'időnként' and 'naponként'.
I can describe rates, speeds, and cost per person (óránként, fejenként).

lessons.title: Role Contrasts & Camp Volunteering
lessons.grammar: Role contrast (-ként vs -nak/-nek vs nominative); narrative
goal: I can contrast -ként, -nak/-nek, and nominative predicate constructions.
I can read and understand a story about summer camp volunteering.

lessons.title: Deferential Politeness: Tetszik + Infinitive
lessons.grammar: Deferential politeness with 'tetszik / tetszenek' + infinitive
goal: I can use the polite 'tetszik + infinitive' form to address elderly people respectfully.
I can offer seats and ask questions politely in shops and transit.

lessons.title: Public Politeness: Tessék, Kérem, Legyen Szíves
lessons.grammar: Polite public formulas: tessék, kérem, parancsoljon, legyen szíves
goal: I can use 'tessék' and 'kérem' appropriately in service and public settings.
I can make polite requests using formal 'legyen szíves' and informal 'légy szíves'.

lessons.title: Name Order & Formal Titles: Kovács Úr, Doktornő
lessons.grammar: Hungarian Eastern name order; honorific titles (úr, nő, -né, bácsi, néni)
goal: I can introduce myself using the Hungarian Eastern name order (family name first).
I can address professionals and older neighbors with appropriate honorific titles.

lessons.title: Name Days and Celebrations: Boldog Névnapot!
lessons.grammar: Name Day greetings; toasting etiquette (koccintás, egészségedre)
goal: I can congratulate someone on their Name Day (névnap) using traditional greetings.
I understand Hungarian toasting etiquette and customs (Egészségedre!, eye contact).

lessons.title: Hungarian Hospitality & Name Day at Grandma's
lessons.grammar: Hungarian visiting and hospitality customs; narrative
goal: I understand Hungarian home visiting etiquette (taking off shoes, gifts, guest slippers).
I can use dining expressions like 'Jó étvágyat kívánok!' and read a family celebration story.

lessons.title: Setting a Scene
lessons.grammar: Scene-setting time words (akkoriban, korábban) and amikor for a whole era
goal: I can open a story by naming when and where it happened.
I can describe the background situation using akkoriban and korábban.
I can use amikor to frame a whole stretch of background time, not just one moment.
I can use four new scene-setting words.

lessons.title: One Thing Led to Another
lessons.grammar: miután + past tense; sequencing connectors deepened (eközben, egymás után)
goal: I can say that one event happened after another using miután + past tense.
I can describe two things happening at the same time using eközben.
I can chain a quick run of events using egymás után.
I can use four new sequencing words.

lessons.title: The Turning Point
lessons.grammar: mielőtt + past tense; combining miután and mielőtt in one narrative
goal: I can say that one event happened before another using mielőtt + past tense.
I can identify which event mielőtt actually marks as later.
I can combine miután and mielőtt in a single sentence to mark a turning point.
I can use four new words for a story's turning point.

lessons.title: How It Ended
lessons.grammar: Closing a story with végül, eredmény and lezár; multi-clause endings
goal: I can close a story using végül and az eredmény az volt, hogy.
I can name what a story's events added up to, not just list them.
I can combine a sequencing connector with a closing word in one sentence.
I can use four new words for a story's ending.

lessons.title: Telling It Well
lessons.grammar: Integrating the storyteller's toolkit; vivid detail with részlet, élénken, lényeg
goal: I can put opening, sequencing, turning point and closing language together in one story.
I can add vivid detail to a story using részlet and élénken.
I can keep a story focused on its lényeg rather than every possible detail.
I can read and understand an adapted Hungarian classic (János vitéz).

lessons.title: Where Hungary Is - Hol van Magyarország?
lessons.grammar: van/vannak a helyhatározásban
goal: I can explain where Hungary is located, using Közép-Európában and a Kárpát-medencében.
I can state Hungary's approximate size and population.
I can explain why Hungarian belongs to the Finno-Ugric language family, unlike most of its neighbours' languages.
I can describe how Budapest relates to the country's counties.
I can use van/vannak correctly when describing where something is located.

lessons.title: Counties, Rivers & Cities - Megyék, folyók és városok
lessons.grammar: Névutók: mellett, mentén, között
goal: I can say how many counties Hungary is divided into, and how Budapest relates to them.
I can name Hungary's two main rivers and explain how they divide the country.
I can describe Lake Balaton and where it lies.
I can name at least four major Hungarian cities and roughly where each one is.
I can use mellett, mentén and között to describe where rivers and cities are relative to each other.

lessons.title: The Flag & the Coat of Arms - A zászló és a címer
lessons.grammar: -ból/-ből áll
goal: I can describe the Hungarian flag's colours and their traditional meaning.
I can describe the two halves of the coat of arms: the Árpád stripes and the triple mound with the crown.
I can explain what the Szent Korona (Holy Crown) is and where it is kept today.
I can explain why the cross on top of the Holy Crown is bent.
I can use -ból/-ből áll to describe what something consists of.

lessons.title: Neighbouring Countries - Magyarország szomszédai
lessons.grammar: határos valamivel + égtájak
goal: I can name Hungary's seven neighbouring countries and roughly where each one is.
I can explain which of Hungary's neighbours are in the EU and Schengen area, and which are not.
I can briefly explain why Hungarian minorities live in several neighbouring countries.
I can use határos valamivel to say that a country borders another.
I can use compass directions with -ra/-re and -tól/-től to say where something lies relative to Hungary.

lessons.title: A First Overview - Első áttekintés
lessons.grammar: Összefoglalás: van/vannak és névutók
goal: I can summarize Hungary's location, size and population in my own words.
I can summarize the country's counties, rivers, regions and major lake.
I can summarize the flag and coat of arms and what they represent.
I can summarize Hungary's neighbouring countries.
I can explain why this basic knowledge matters for the honosítási vizsga (naturalization interview).

lessons.title: Have You Ever...?
lessons.grammar: Experiential aspect with már (already/ever) and még soha nem (never yet) + past tense
goal: I can say I've already had an experience using már + past tense.
I can say I've never had an experience yet using még soha nem + past tense.
I can ask someone if they have ever done something using már and valaha.
I can use four new words for talking about experiences.

lessons.title: My First Time
lessons.grammar: Marking a first-time event with (életemben) először; feelings around a first experience
goal: I can mark an event as a first-time experience using először and életemben először.
I can distinguish a one-time first-time narration from a general már-experience.
I can describe my feelings before trying something new for the first time.
I can use four new words for first-time experiences.

lessons.title: A Memory That Stayed With Me
lessons.grammar: Past participle as an adjective (elkészített étel); describing the impression a memory left
goal: I can form a past participle from a verb and use it as an adjective, like elkészített étel.
I can use past-participle adjectives to describe people and things shaped by something that happened to them.
I can describe the impression a memory left on me.
I can use four new words for describing a vivid memory.

lessons.title: Looking Back
lessons.grammar: Reflecting on change with azelőtt/azóta/megváltozik; visszatekint + -ra/-re
goal: I can frame a reflection on the past using visszatekintve and the pattern visszatekintek valamire.
I can say how I've changed using megváltozik, and describe what came before with azelőtt and after with azóta.
I can combine looking-back language with past-participle adjectives in one sentence.
I can use four new words for reflecting on change.

lessons.title: Comparing Experiences
lessons.grammar: Integrating the experience toolkit; comparing with képest, egyre + comparative, mint
goal: I can put experiential már/még soha, first-time framing, participle adjectives and looking-back language together in one reflection.
I can compare an experience to another using képest and comparative adjectives.
I can say something is increasingly true using egyre + comparative.
I can read and understand an adapted Hungarian classic (Hét krajcár).

units.title: The Carpathian Basin Before the Magyars

lessons.title: Early Peoples of the Basin - A medence korai népei
lessons.grammar: Több szereplő a múlt idejű elbeszélésben
goal: I can name at least three peoples who lived in the Carpathian Basin before the Romans arrived, including the Celts.
I can explain where the name 'Pannónia' comes from.
I can describe the Celtic Eravisci tribe and their settlement near today's Budapest.
I can correctly match singular and plural verb endings when several different historical subjects appear in one narrative.
I can describe how the Celts were gradually absorbed by the peoples who arrived after them.

lessons.title: The Roman Province of Pannonia - Pannónia, a római tartomány
lessons.grammar: Sorrend a történelemben: korábban, majd, végül
goal: I can explain when and how the Romans conquered the western part of the Carpathian Basin.
I can name at least three Roman cities founded in Pannonia and their modern equivalents.
I can describe what life was like in the Roman province of Pannonia.
I can explain why and when the Romans withdrew from Pannonia.
I can use korábban, majd and végül to sequence events in a historical narrative.

lessons.title: The Great Migrations - A népvándorlás kora
lessons.grammar: míg — egyidejű események
goal: I can explain what the népvándorlás (Migration Period) was.
I can name the main peoples who moved through or settled in the Carpathian Basin during the Migration Period: the Huns, Goths, Avars and Slavs.
I can describe the rise and fall of the Hun and Avar powers in the basin.
I can use míg to describe two things happening at the same time.
I can explain that the Avars and Slavic peoples coexisted in different parts of the basin at the same time.

lessons.title: Who Lived Here Before - Kik éltek itt korábban?
lessons.grammar: Több szereplő és míg: összetett történelmi mondatok
goal: I can summarize, in my own words, which peoples lived in the Carpathian Basin before the Magyars, in the order they arrived.
I can explain why no single people controlled the whole Carpathian Basin before 895.
I can describe how earlier peoples' influence survived even after their political power disappeared.
I can combine multiple historical subjects and míg clauses in a single complex sentence.
I can answer the question 'Who lived here before the Magyars?' with a clear, connected explanation.

lessons.title: Setting the Scene for 895 - A honfoglalás előestéjén
lessons.grammar: Összefoglalás: több szereplő, sorrend és míg
goal: I can describe the political situation in the Carpathian Basin at the end of the 9th century, after the fall of the Avar Khaganate.
I can explain why the open, sparsely settled plains of the basin suited a nomadic, horse-based people.
I can explain what the honfoglalás means and why it happened around 895.
I can describe the Magyar tribal confederation setting out to find a new homeland, without narrating the crossing itself.
I can use multi-subject narration, sequencing words and míg clauses together to summarize this unit's history.

lessons.title: Where I See Myself
lessons.grammar: szeretném vs. szeretnék (definite/indefinite conditional); szeretném, ha + conditional
goal: I can tell szeretném and szeretnék apart, and use the definite conditional for a specific wish.
I can use szeretném, ha + conditional to say what I wish would happen.
I can talk about where I see myself in the future using elképzel and jövőkép.
I can use four new words for imagining my future self.

lessons.title: I Wish I Could...
lessons.grammar: bárcsak + conditional; szeretném, ha + conditional matched to te/ő
goal: I can make an emphatic wish with bárcsak + conditional.
I can use szeretném, ha to wish for something about someone else, matching the conditional to te or ő.
I can talk about dreams and wishes coming true using álom and megvalósul.
I can use four new words for wishes and dreams.

lessons.title: Steps Toward a Goal
lessons.grammar: The -jon/-jen form; hogy + -jon/-jen after wanting-verbs (akar, szeretné)
goal: I can form the -jon/-jen third-person command and subjunctive form of a verb.
I can use hogy + -jon/-jen after verbs like akar and szeretné to say what I want to happen.
I can talk about the steps and progress toward a goal using lépés, fejlődés and kitartás.
I can use four new words for steps and progress toward a goal.

lessons.title: What Might Stop Me
lessons.grammar: azért, hogy + -jon/-jen (purpose clauses); nehogy + -jon/-jen (negative purpose)
goal: I can explain the purpose of an action using azért, hogy + -jon/-jen.
I can say what I'm doing to prevent something using nehogy + -jon/-jen.
I can talk about obstacles and setbacks using akadály, nehézség, kockázat and kétség.
I can use four new words for obstacles and doubts.

lessons.title: My Five-Year Plan
lessons.grammar: Combining szeretném, ha and azért, hogy; annak érdekében, hogy as a formal synonym
goal: I can combine szeretném, ha and azért, hogy in one longer sentence about my plans.
I can use the more formal annak érdekében, hogy as a synonym for azért, hogy.
I can talk about long-term goals using megvalósít, hosszú távú, mérföldkő and elköteleződik.
I can read and understand an adapted Hungarian classic (Az arany ember).

lessons.title: Why the Magyar Tribes Migrated West - Miért indultak nyugatra a magyar törzsek
lessons.grammar: Miután és mielőtt: sorrend mellékmondatokkal
goal: I can explain why the Magyar tribes migrated west, including the role of Pecheneg pressure and the weakening of their Khazar allies.
I can name Etelköz as the territory the Magyar tribes left before 895.
I can use miután and mielőtt to sequence cause and effect in a historical narrative.
I can describe the Magyar tribes' earlier life on the Pontic steppe in a sentence or two.
I can explain that this kind of migration under pressure from a neighboring people also happened earlier in the region's history.

lessons.title: Crossing the Carpathians - Átkelés a Kárpátokon
lessons.grammar: Miután, mielőtt, majd, végül együtt
goal: I can describe how the Magyar tribes crossed the Carpathian mountains around 895.
I can name the Vereckei-hágó as the pass tradition associates with the crossing, while noting other routes were also used.
I can describe the bow and arrow as the key weapons of Magyar warriors and explain their military advantage.
I can combine miután, mielőtt, majd and végül to narrate a longer sequence of events.
I can explain that the tribes did not all cross by the same route or at exactly the same time.

lessons.title: Árpád & the Seven Tribes - Árpád és a hét törzs
lessons.grammar: Nevesített alanyok: Árpád és a hét törzs
goal: I can explain the traditional account of the vérszerződés, the blood oath among the seven tribal chieftains.
I can name Árpád as the leader who brought the tribes into the Carpathian Basin and founded the Árpád dynasty.
I can distinguish singular verb forms for a named individual (Árpád) from plural verb forms for the tribes as a group.
I can mention the kabarok as an eighth group that joined the seven Magyar tribes.
I can use the 3rd-person-plural construction to express a passive-like meaning, such as 'Árpádot fejedelemmé választották.'

lessons.title: Settling the Basin - A medence birtokba vétele
lessons.grammar: Több szereplő és miután/mielőtt összekapcsolva
goal: I can describe how the Magyar tribes gradually occupied the Carpathian Basin over several years rather than all at once.
I can explain how the Slavic tribes and Avar remnants already living in the basin were displaced, absorbed, or made to pay tribute.
I can name the Battle of Pozsony (907) as the victory that secured the new homeland.
I can combine miután/mielőtt with multiple named and collective subjects in one sentence.
I can explain why the Alföld's open grassland suited the Magyars' nomadic, horse-based economy.

lessons.title: The Honfoglalás in National Memory - A honfoglalás a nemzeti emlékezetben
lessons.grammar: Összefoglalás: miután, mielőtt és több szereplő
goal: I can explain why 895 and the honfoglalás matter to Hungarian national identity today, including for the citizenship exam.
I can name the turul bird and the Csodaszarvas legend as part of the honfoglalás's place in national memory.
I can describe the Millennium Monument at Hősök tere and what it commemorates.
I can explain that the honfoglalás has no dedicated state holiday, unlike August 20th.
I can combine miután, mielőtt and multi-subject narration to summarize this unit's history fluently.

lessons.title: If I Were You
lessons.grammar: Giving advice with a helyedben and the full ha (én) a helyedben lennék hypothetical
goal: I can give advice by imagining myself in someone else's place using a helyedben + conditional.
I can spell out the full hypothetical with ha (én) a helyedben lennék.
I can conjugate the advice-giving verb for myself (én), not for the person I'm advising.
I can use four new words for talking about uncertain, tricky situations.

lessons.title: You'd Better...
lessons.grammar: -hat/-het + conditional as a softened suggestion; jobb lenne, ha for "you'd better"
goal: I can soften a suggestion using -hat/-het + conditional, like kipróbálhatnád.
I can say what would be better for someone using jobb lenne, ha + conditional.
I can tell the difference between a direct command and a gentle suggestion in Hungarian.
I can use four new words for weighing when and whether to act.

lessons.title: Weighing Two Options
lessons.grammar: egyrészt... másrészt... for advantages/disadvantages; inkább... mint... + conditional for a gentle preference
goal: I can lay out an advantage and a disadvantage side by side using egyrészt... másrészt...
I can state a gentle preference between two options using inkább... mint... + conditional.
I can help someone weigh a choice without deciding it for them.
I can use four new words for advantages, disadvantages and weighing options.

lessons.title: Gentle Warnings
lessons.grammar: nehogy + imperative for a caring warning; -hat/-het naming a possible risk or consequence
goal: I can warn someone caringly, not to do something, using nehogy + imperative.
I can name a possible bad outcome gently using -hat/-het, like megbánhatod.
I can tell the difference between a flat prohibition and a worried warning.
I can use four new words for talking about danger, risk and consequences.

lessons.title: Talking Someone Through a Problem
lessons.grammar: Integrating the full advice toolkit; talking-someone-into/out-of verbs (rábeszél, lebeszél, meggyőz, bátorít)
goal: I can combine this unit's advice tools — a helyedben, -hat/-het suggestions, egyrészt/másrészt, nehogy — in one conversation.
I can talk about persuading, discouraging, convincing and encouraging someone using four new verbs.
I can walk a friend through weighing a real dilemma from start to finish.
I can read and understand an adapted Hungarian classic about giving advice.

units.title: Saint Stephen & the Founding of the State (1000)

lessons.title: Prince Géza & the Turn to Christianity - Géza fejedelem és a kereszténység felé fordulás
lessons.grammar: Melléknévi igenév: történelmi jelzők
goal: I can explain why Prince Géza sought closer ties with the Christian world in the late 10th century.
I can describe how Géza had his son baptized, and that the boy took the name István (Stephen).
I can name Bajor Gizella (Gisela of Bavaria) as the wife the young István married, strengthening ties with the West.
I can use the past participle as an adjective to form historical epithets like 'megkeresztelt fejedelem'.
I can describe how Christianity gradually spread among the Magyars during Géza's rule.

lessons.title: István's Coronation - István koronázása
lessons.grammar: A megkoronázott király
goal: I can explain that after Géza's death, István had to defend his succession against the pagan chieftain Koppány.
I can describe when and how István was crowned the first King of Hungary, around the year 1000.
I can explain the tradition that Pope Sylvester II sent István his crown, recognizing Hungary as a Christian kingdom in its own right.
I can use participle titles like 'megkoronázott király' and 'felkent uralkodó' to describe a monarch.
I can explain why István's coronation is considered the founding moment of the Hungarian state.

lessons.title: Building a Christian Kingdom - Keresztény királyság építése
lessons.grammar: Melléknévi igenév: alapított intézmények
goal: I can describe how István organized the Hungarian church, establishing an archbishopric and ten dioceses.
I can explain the tradition that every ten villages had to build a church.
I can describe how István's laws protected Christian practice and punished a return to paganism.
I can use participle titles like 'alapított kolostor' and 'bevezetett törvény' to describe institutions.
I can explain how István built a functioning Christian kingdom, not just won a single battle.

lessons.title: Saint Stephen's Legacy - Szent István öröksége
lessons.grammar: Melléknévi igenév: szentté avatott örökség
goal: I can explain what the Intelmek (Admonitions) were, and to whom István addressed them.
I can describe István's death in 1038 and the succession crisis that followed his son Imre's early death.
I can explain that István was canonized in 1083 and became Hungary's patron saint.
I can use participle titles like 'szentté avatott király' to describe his sainthood.
I can explain why August 20th honors Saint Stephen as Hungary's state-founder.

lessons.title: The Holy Crown - A Szent Korona
lessons.grammar: Összefoglalás: melléknévi igenév és 'által'
goal: I can name the parts of the Hungarian coronation regalia: the crown, the scepter, the orb and the mantle.
I can describe the Holy Crown's eventful modern history, including its return to Hungary in 1978.
I can explain what the Holy Crown symbolizes today: the continuity of Hungarian statehood.
I can combine participle titles with 'által' agent phrases, e.g. 'a pápa által küldött korona'.
I can connect Szent István's coronation to the founding of the Árpád royal dynasty that followed him.

lessons.title: How We Get Along
lessons.grammar: Reciprocal egymás; kijönnek egymással for describing how well people get along
goal: I can say what people do to or with each other using egymás.
I can say how well people get along using kijönnek egymással.
I can use four new words for talking about relationships in general.
I can describe a relationship's basic dynamic in a few sentences.

lessons.title: Falling Out and Making Up
lessons.grammar: veszekedik/összevész for conflict; kibékül/megbocsát for making up
goal: I can talk about arguing and falling out with veszekedik and összevész.
I can talk about making up and forgiving with kibékül and megbocsát.
I can use four new words for the shape of a conflict and its resolution.
I can tell a short story about a falling-out and how it ended.

lessons.title: Supporting Each Other
lessons.grammar: Reflexive support verbs (gondoskodik, támaszkodik, ragaszkodik); segítenek egymásnak, számítanak egymásra
goal: I can talk about caring for, relying on, and being attached to someone with gondoskodik, támaszkodik and ragaszkodik.
I can say that people help and count on each other using segítenek egymásnak and számítanak egymásra.
I can use four new words for support and trust in a relationship.
I can describe how two people support each other.

lessons.title: Describing a Friendship
lessons.grammar: annak ellenére, hogy (concession); olyan barát, aki... (aki-relative describing a friend)
goal: I can concede a contrast with annak ellenére, hogy — "despite the fact that".
I can describe a friend with an aki-clause, like olyan barát, aki mindig meghallgat.
I can use four new words for describing what a friendship is like.
I can describe a friendship, including something that's true despite something else.

lessons.title: What Makes a Relationship Work
lessons.grammar: Integrating the relationship toolkit: egymás, conflict/making-up verbs, reflexive support verbs, annak ellenére hogy, aki-descriptions
goal: I can put this unit's relationship language together — egymás, conflict and making-up verbs, support verbs, annak ellenére hogy, and aki-descriptions.
I can explain what makes a relationship work, including its ups and downs.
I can use four new words for compromise and steady care over time.
I can read and understand an adapted Hungarian classic about friendship.

lessons.title: Kings of the Árpád Line - Az Árpád-házi királyok
lessons.grammar: A vonatkozói mellékmondat: aki
goal: I can name the Árpád dynasty as Hungary's founding royal house, descended from Árpád.
I can describe at least two notable kings who ruled after István: I. László (Saint Ladislaus) and Könyves Kálmán (Coloman the Learned).
I can explain who II. András was and what he is best known for.
I can use the relative clause 'aki' to describe a king with a defining action ('X, aki Y-t tett, ...').
I can list several Árpád-house rulers in sequence using aki-clauses.

lessons.title: The Golden Bull (1222) - Az Aranybulla (1222)
lessons.grammar: aki és amely: személyek és dolgok
goal: I can explain what the Aranybulla (Golden Bull) of 1222 was and who issued it.
I can describe why the Hungarian nobility pressed II. András to issue the Golden Bull.
I can name at least two rights the Golden Bull guaranteed and briefly compare it to England's Magna Carta.
I can distinguish 'aki' (for people) from 'amely' (for things) in a relative clause.
