I can build a sentence combining a person clause (aki) and a thing clause (amely) about the same event.

lessons.title: Consolidating the Kingdom - Az ország megszervezése
lessons.grammar: A vonatkozó névmás esetei: akit, akinek, akik
goal: I can describe how the counties (vármegyék) and royal officials (ispánok) organized the kingdom.
I can explain what the tatárjárás (Mongol invasion of 1241-42) was and its main consequences.
I can describe IV. Béla's post-invasion reconstruction, including stone castle building.
I can use the case-marked relative pronouns akit, akinek and akik correctly.
I can describe a historical figure using a relative clause in an oblique case ('a király, akinek...').

lessons.title: Church & State - Egyház és állam
lessons.grammar: ahol és amikor: hely- és időhatározói mellékmondatok
goal: I can describe how the Christian church was organized in the kingdom: dioceses, archbishops, bishops and monasteries.
I can explain the relationship between the Árpád-house kings and the Church, including canonizations.
I can name Pannonhalma as an early and important monastery.
I can use the relative adverbs 'ahol' and 'amikor' to describe places and times.
I can combine 'aki', 'amely', 'ahol' and 'amikor' clauses to describe church-related history.

lessons.title: The End of the Árpád Line - Az Árpád-ház vége
lessons.grammar: Összefoglalás: vonatkozói mellékmondatok
goal: I can explain what 'fiúág' means and why it mattered for royal succession.
I can describe III. András and explain why he was the last Árpád-house king.
I can explain what happened in 1301 and why it mattered for Hungary's history.
I can describe the power struggles among magnates (főurak) in the kingdom's late Árpád period.
I can combine relative clauses fluently to summarize the Árpád dynasty's rise and fall.

lessons.title: A Typical Workday, in Detail
lessons.grammar: Present participle -ó/-ő as adjective; workday schedules and overtime (munkaidőben, túlórázik)
goal: I can form and use the present participle -ó/-ő as an adjective.
I can describe my daily work schedule from start to finish.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to office roles and schedules.
I can discuss workday habits, duties, and overtime in natural Hungarian.

lessons.title: Responsibilities & Tasks Done
lessons.grammar: Passive-avoidance verbs in -ódik/-ődik (megoldódik, befejeződik); stating responsibilities (felelős valamiért)
goal: I can use mediopassive verbs ending in -ódik/-ődik to describe events unfolding.
I can state professional responsibilities using felelős valamiért.
I can use four new words for managing tasks and solving problems.
I can describe when and how tasks get completed.

lessons.title: Applying for a Job
lessons.grammar: Formal application structures (pályázik/jelentkezik vmire); expressing suitability (alkalmas, megfelel)
goal: I can use formal verbs for applying to a position (jelentkezik, pályázik).
I can state why I meet job requirements using megfelel and alkalmas.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to recruitment and CVs.
I can introduce myself and my strengths in an interview setting.

lessons.title: Office Life
lessons.grammar: Meeting collocations (megbeszélést tart, egyeztet vkivel); handling deadlines (határidő, késésben van)
goal: I can coordinate tasks and meetings with colleagues using egyeztet.
I can talk about keeping and missing deadlines using határidő and késésben van.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to office collaboration.
I can discuss everyday problems and solutions at work.

lessons.title: Talking About My Career
lessons.grammar: Synthesizing career & professional growth expressions (karriert épít, tapasztalatot szerez, előléptetés)
goal: I can discuss my career trajectory and professional development.
I can use collocations like tapasztalatot szerez and karriert épít.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to professional growth.
I can read and understand an adapted Hungarian classic about office politics and ethics.

lessons.title: The Mongols Arrive - Megérkeznek a tatárok
lessons.grammar: Verbs of warning and approach: közeledik, figyelmeztet, betör
goal: I can describe the approaching Mongol threat in the 1230s and Julianus barát's mission.
I can explain why King IV. Béla settled the fleeing Cumans in Hungary.
I can use verbs of warning and approach (figyelmeztet, közeledik, betör).
I can discuss how the Hungarian nobility reacted to the impending danger.

lessons.title: The Battle of Mohi - A muhi csata
lessons.grammar: Battle verbs & clashing forces: megütközik, vereséget szenved, elmenekül
goal: I can state the exact date (1241. április 11.) and location (Sajó folyó, Muhi) of the battle.
I can describe the wagon fort (szekérvár) tactic and why it failed.
I can use battle verbs like megütközik, vereséget szenved, and elmenekül.
I can recount the escape of King Béla IV.

lessons.title: A Kingdom Devastated - Egy elpusztult ország
lessons.grammar: Mediopassive & destruction verbs: elpusztul, romba dől, felég, megsemmisül
goal: I can describe the winter crossing of the frozen Danube by the Mongols.
I can explain Rogerius mester's Carmen Miserabile and its historical significance.
I can use mediopassive destruction verbs (elpusztul, romba dől, felég).
I can recount IV. Béla's refuge in the island fortress of Trau (Trogir).

lessons.title: Béla IV & the Rebuilding - IV. Béla és az újjáépítés
lessons.grammar: Rebuilding & settlement verbs: újjáépít, letelepít, behív, visszatér
goal: I can explain why the Mongols abruptly left Hungary in spring 1242.
I can describe IV. Béla's estate and settlement policies.
I can explain why IV. Béla is called the 'Second Founder of the State'.
I can use verbs with the prefix újjá- and settlement terms.

lessons.title: The Stone Castles - A kővárak
lessons.grammar: Defensive fortifications & condition: kővárat épít, védelmet nyújt, ellenáll
goal: I can explain why stone castles succeeded against the Mongols where earthworks failed.
I can name key fortifications founded by IV. Béla (Buda Castle, Visegrád).
I can explain the outcome of the 1285 second Tatar invasion.
I can use defense collocations (kővárat épít, védelmet nyújt, ellenáll).

lessons.title: The Hungarian School System
lessons.grammar: Potential suffix -hat/-het in institutional rules; schooling stages (általános iskola, gimnázium)
goal: I can explain the main stages of the Hungarian education system.
I can use the -hat/-het potential suffix to describe what students may or can do.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to schools and qualifications.
I can discuss admission requirements and graduation exams in natural Hungarian.

lessons.title: Why I'm Learning This
lessons.grammar: Purpose clauses: azért, hogy + subjunctive; expressing personal motivations
goal: I can express purpose and goals using azért, hogy + subjunctive.
I can explain why I am studying Hungarian or professional subjects.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to objectives and skill development.
I can discuss long-term training plans with peers.

lessons.title: Studying Effectively
lessons.grammar: Verbs of attention & note-taking (összpontosít vmire, jegyzetel)
goal: I can discuss effective study techniques, focus, and memory.
I can use verbs with their proper noun cases like összpontosít valamire.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to study methods and revision.
I can advise someone on how to organize their study schedule.

lessons.title: Exams & Results
lessons.grammar: Exam result collocations: átmegy a vizsgán, megbukik, érdemjegyet kap
goal: I can describe exam preparation, taking an exam, and results.
I can distinguish between oral (szóbeli) and written (írásbeli) examinations.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to grades and certificates.
I can talk about the Hungarian 1-to-5 grading scale comfortably.

lessons.title: Lifelong Learning
lessons.grammar: Synthesis: adult education, retraining, and lifelong curiosity
goal: I can discuss lifelong learning, retraining, and personal development.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to adult education.
I can express complex aspirations and educational opportunities.
I can read and understand an adapted excerpt from Karinthy's Tanár úr kérem.

lessons.title: Charles Robert & Financial Stability - Károly Róbert és a gazdasági rend
lessons.grammar: Chronicler reported speech: A krónikák szerint, úgy tartják, hogy...
goal: I can describe the rise of Charles Robert and the defeat of the oligarchs (kiskirályok).
I can explain the economic significance of Körmöcbánya mining and the gold florin (aranyforint).
I can use chronicler reporting expressions (a krónikák szerint, úgy tartják).
I can use eight new vocabulary items related to medieval finance and royal authority.

lessons.title: The Congress of Visegrád 1335 - A visegrádi királytalálkozó
lessons.grammar: Diplomatic agreement reporting: megállapodtak abban, hogy...
goal: I can describe the 1335 Congress of Visegrád and its participants.
I can explain the commercial purpose of bypassing Vienna's staple right.
I can use diplomatic reporting phrases like megállapodtak abban, hogy.
I can connect the 1335 summit with today's Visegrád Group (V4).

lessons.title: Louis the Great & the Laws of 1351 - Nagy Lajos és az 1351-es törvények
lessons.grammar: Epithets & law enactments: úgy nevezték, mint; megerősítette a törvényt
goal: I can explain why Louis I is remembered as Louis the Great and the knight-king (lovagkirály).
I can describe the 1351 renewal of the Golden Bull and the law of entailment (ősiség).
I can explain the feudal ninth tax (kilenced) paid by serfs.
I can discuss the Polish-Hungarian personal union established in 1370.

lessons.title: Sigismund & the Ottoman Threat - Zsigmond és az oszmán veszély
lessons.grammar: Threats & border fortifications: fenyeget, kiépít, végvárrendszer
goal: I can outline Sigismund of Luxembourg's reign as king and Holy Roman Emperor.
I can explain the rising Ottoman threat following the 1396 Battle of Nicopolis.
I can describe the creation of the southern border defense system (végvárrendszer).
I can use defense and warfare vocabulary (császár, hadjárat, végvár).

lessons.title: János Hunyadi & the Victory at Nándorfehérvár - Hunyadi János és a nándorfehérvári diadal
lessons.grammar: Commemorative synthesis: azóta hirdeti, emlékére, tiszteletére
goal: I can narrate the siege and triumph of Belgrade / Nándorfehérvár in July 1456.
I can describe János Hunyadi's leadership as regent and 'Turk-beater' (törökverő).
I can explain the historical origin of the worldwide midday church bells (déli harangszó).
I can confidently answer citizenship interview questions about Nándorfehérvár and Hunyadi.

lessons.title: Getting There
lessons.grammar: Postpositions of motion: keresztül, át, felé, felől; public transport navigation
goal: I can navigate public transport schedules, transfers, and destinations.
I can use spatial postpositions of motion like felé and felől.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to transit and journeys.
I can ask for directions and transfer information at train stations.

lessons.title: Through, Across, Toward
lessons.grammar: Verbal prefixes of motion (át-, be-, le-) with terrain nouns and postposition keresztül
goal: I can describe moving through geographical terrain, tunnels, and passes.
I can combine motion prefixes (átkel, áthalad) with postpositions like keresztül.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to landscape and topography.
I can read and give trail and road descriptions using a map.

lessons.title: Until When, From When
lessons.grammar: Terminative case -ig in space and time; travel duration expressions
goal: I can use the terminative case -ig to specify destinations and time limits.
I can discuss departure, arrival, duration, and delays accurately.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to scheduling and journey time.
I can understand and calculate travel time differences.

lessons.title: When Travel Goes Wrong
lessons.grammar: Travel mishaps and problem resolution: lekésik, pótlóbusz, panaszt tesz
goal: I can handle unexpected travel disruptions, missed trains, and delays.
I can describe lost luggage and file complaints at customer service.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to railway problems.
I can ask about alternative routes and replacement buses (pótlóbusz).

lessons.title: Planning a Trip
lessons.grammar: Synthesis: complete trip planning, itineraries, bookings, and regional exploration
goal: I can prepare a full travel itinerary, reserve accommodation, and select sights.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to vacation planning.
I can express recommendations for exploring Hungarian towns and regions.
I can read and understand an adapted excerpt from Mikszáth's Szent Péter esernyője.

lessons.title: The Election of Matthias - Mátyás megválasztása
lessons.grammar: Superlative & absolute comparisons: legfiatalabb, egyik legjelentősebb
goal: I can narrate the dramatic January 1458 election of young Matthias on the frozen Danube.
I can explain the origin of the Corvinus name and the raven emblem with the gold ring.
I can use superlative and absolute comparative structures in historical descriptions.
I can use eight new vocabulary items related to medieval coronations and monarchical succession.

lessons.title: The Black Army - A fekete sereg
lessons.grammar: Correlative comparisons: minél ..., annál ...
goal: I can describe the composition, discipline, and weaponry of Matthias's Black Army (fekete sereg).
I can explain why creating a professional standing army was revolutionary in 15th-century Europe.
I can use correlative comparative sentences (minél fegyelmezettebb, annál sikeresebb).
I can discuss Matthias's military campaigns, border defense, and the 1485 capture of Vienna.

lessons.title: A Renaissance Court in Buda - Reneszánsz udvar Budán
lessons.grammar: Cultural flourishing & patronage: virágzott, meghonosodott, felvirágoztat
goal: I can explain why Hungary was the first country outside Italy to adopt Renaissance art and humanism.
I can describe the Bibliotheca Corviniana and the cultural significance of the Corvina codices.
I can describe the palaces at Buda and Visegrád, their red marble fountains, and hanging gardens.
I can use eight new vocabulary items related to Renaissance scholarship, literature, and art.

lessons.title: Justice & Good Government - Mátyás, az igazságos
lessons.grammar: Folktale framing: a mesék szerint, álruhában járta az országot
goal: I can explain why King Matthias earned the popular title 'Matthias the Just' (Mátyás, az igazságos).
I can describe the folklore motif of the king traveling among the people in disguise (álruhában).
I can explain Matthias's fiscal reform: replacing the gate tax with the chimney tax (füstadó).
I can use eight new vocabulary items related to taxation, justice, and folklore traditions.

lessons.title: "King Matthias Is Dead, Justice Has Perished" - Meghalt Mátyás, oda az igazság
lessons.grammar: Proverbs & collective memorial: Meghalt Mátyás, oda az igazság
goal: I can explain the circumstances of King Matthias's sudden death in Vienna in 1490.
I can analyze the famous proverb 'Meghalt Mátyás, oda az igazság' and its cultural resonance.
I can outline what happened to Hungary following 1490: dissolution of the Black Army and decline.
I can confidently answer citizenship interview questions regarding Matthias's golden age.

lessons.title: One Should...
lessons.grammar: Impersonal general subject 'az ember'; full modal paradigm (kell, lehet)
goal: I can express generalized health advice and truths using az ember.
I can use modals like kell and lehet with dative subjects.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to lifestyle and nutrition.
I can discuss prevention and healthy daily habits.

lessons.title: It's Not Allowed To...
lessons.grammar: Prohibitions and permissions: szabad, tilos, nem szabad; moderation
goal: I can express strict prohibitions and permissions using szabad and tilos.
I can discuss harmful habits and the principle of moderation (mérték).
I can use four new vocabulary items related to consumption and habits.
I can understand health warnings and public health signs in Hungary.

lessons.title: At the Doctor's, in Detail
lessons.grammar: Doctor-patient interactions: panaszkodik vmire, felír, kivált
goal: I can describe medical symptoms and complaints clearly to a physician.
I can understand doctors' examination instructions and prescriptions.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to clinics and pharmacies.
I can navigate picking up prescription medicine at a Hungarian pharmacy.

lessons.title: Stress & Balance
lessons.grammar: Mental wellness collocations: feszültséget levezet, egyensúlyt talál
goal: I can discuss stress management, work-life balance, and relaxation.
I can use collocations like feszültséget levezet and egyensúlyt tart.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to mental wellbeing.
I can describe relaxing activities and active recovery techniques.

lessons.title: Giving Health Advice
lessons.grammar: Synthesis: gentle health advice with érdemes, ajánlott, tanácsos
goal: I can offer polite, natural health advice using érdemes and ajánlott.
I can discuss treatments, medical therapies, and complete recovery.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to wellbeing and healing.
I can read and understand an adapted literary excerpt from Kosztolányi's Esti Kornél.

lessons.title: A meggyengült királyság (The Weakened Kingdom)
lessons.grammar: Causality & Preconditions: miatt, következtében, eredményeképpen
goal: I can describe the domestic political and financial crisis in Hungary after King Matthias's death.
I can explain the impact of the 1514 Dózsa peasant revolt on social unity.
I can express complex historical causes using postpositions: miatt, következtében, eredményeképpen.
I can master eight new vocabulary items related to internal strife and feudal discord.

lessons.title: Az oszmán előrenyomulás (The Ottoman Advance)
lessons.grammar: Temporal Conjunctions: amikor, miután, mielőtt
goal: I can describe the rise of Sultan Suleiman I and his military offensive against Hungary.
I can explain the strategic catastrophe of the fall of Nándorfehérvár in 1521.
I can construct chronological military narratives using amikor, miután, and mielőtt.
I can use eight new vocabulary items related to siegecraft and Ottoman expansion.

lessons.title: A csata lefolyása (The Battle of Mohács)
lessons.grammar: Rapid Succession & Tactical Sequence: alighogy... máris, rövid idő alatt
goal: I can recount the course of the Battle of Mohács on August 29, 1526.
I can identify Archbishop Pál Tomori and his tactical choices during the battle.
I can express rapid sequences and tactical shifts using alighogy... máris and hirtelen.
I can utilize eight new vocabulary items concerning battlefield orders and cavalry charges.

lessons.title: A király halála (The King's Death)
lessons.grammar: Past Participles in Tragedy: megfulladt, elhunyt, menekülő
goal: I can narrate the tragedy of King Louis II in the swollen Csele brook.
I can explain the dynastic crisis and double king election caused by his childless demise.
I can use attributive and predicative past participles to describe historical events.
I can deploy eight new vocabulary items regarding royal demise and political succession.

lessons.title: Miért fontos Mohács ma is? (Why Mohács Matters Today)
lessons.grammar: Proverbs & Fatalism: Több is veszett Mohácsnál
goal: I can explain the cultural meaning and usage of 'Több is veszett Mohácsnál'.
I can articulate why August 29, 1526, is seen as the end of the medieval Hungarian state.
I can discuss the Mohács National Memorial Site (Mohácsi Nemzeti Emlékhely).
I can answer citizenship interview questions about Mohács with high historical accuracy.

lessons.title: Turning a House into a Home
lessons.grammar: Translative Case -vá / -vé & Transformation Verbs (válik, tesz)
goal: I can express transformation and change of state using the translative case -vá / -vé.
I can describe home remodeling, renovation, and interior improvements.
I can contrast intransitive válik with transitive tesz in transformation clauses.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to ambiance, lighting, and renovation.

lessons.title: The Place I Live In
lessons.grammar: Relative Pronouns with Places & Inanimates: amely, amiben, ahol
goal: I can connect descriptive details of dwellings using relative pronouns (amely, amiben, ahol).
I can distinguish between detached homes (családi ház) and apartments (társasház).
I can discuss balconies, yards, and common condominium features.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to residential property types.

lessons.title: Renting & Tenancy Agreements
lessons.grammar: Contractual Clauses: köteles, jogosult, esetén
goal: I can understand and discuss terms in a rental lease (bérleti szerződés).
I can negotiate security deposits (kaució) and utility payments (rezsi) with a landlord.
I can express rights and contractual duties using köteles, jogosult, and esetén.
I can use four new vocabulary items related to leases and rental management.

lessons.title: Interior Layout & Spatial Relations
